# probes/install/ir/capture-stage2-callees.sh; do not edit.
# Every place the capture *rewrote* a token of the emission instead of
# removing it, with the reason the rewrite is sound.  Two kinds:
#   substituted  a token replaced by a defined one: `poison`, the class
#                `capture-escape.sh` records for the hex reader's two
#                vector constants.  `num_d8_el1`'s three literal vectors
#                carry it in lanes the body overwrites (the
#                `insertelement`'s lane 0) or whose results the body never
#                reads (the `pmadd` constants' upper lanes), so the defined
#                lane 0 stands in.
#   weakened     a token replaced by one that promises less: the second
#                argument of `num_el_el1`'s one `llvm.ctlz.i64` call is
#                written `i1 true` and held as `i1 false`.  LLVM's flag
#                `true` makes the zero word poison and licenses the
#                optimizer to assume a nonzero operand; the parser admits
#                only `false`, which returns the width at zero, so the
#                fixture states the weaker promise.  The entry's
#                `%w == 0` return keeps the zero word off the only path to
#                the call, so the two flags denote the same value wherever
#                the body executes.
# The `from` column is the emitted token, the `to` column the one the
# fixture holds, and `line` is the line of the extracted body.  The
# `class` column is the normalisation class where the row is one of
# `capture-escape.sh`'s (the `poison` substitution is class 6), and
# `n/a` where the row is this capture's own rewrite (`weakened`).
# A callee with no row is a body the capture did not rewrite.  `stk_mul_u64`
# and `stk_cmp` are such bodies: the strip removes surface, and neither
# needs a token substituted or weakened.
